svg.text: The approach: agreement is the work; prepare before you write (boring ideas, join expeditions, sponsor, core group, scope, achievability), then make it official
Embrace the boring ideas
most strategy is synthesis, not genius; the gap is getting everyone to agree; weigh
options, make the case, be brave enough to decide (Camille Fournier, Will Larson)
Join an expedition in progress
share the lead, follow their lead, or step away; avoid 'ape games'; just because it
came from your brain is not best (Robert Konigsberg); join and redirect rather than
compete
Get a sponsor
a director or VP who can fund and staff, set success criteria, break ties or name a
DRI; bring what they want; practise a 50-word pitch (Melissa Binde's coaching);
keep the sponsorship alive; a staff+ engineer cannot sponsor
Choose a core group
two to four people with a time commitment (8 to 12 hours a week) to keep tourists
out; wider allies get interviews and early drafts; say who is lead and tiebreaker;
let the group drive
Set scope and document type
enough ground to solve the problem; include someone from any team you touch; no
magical thinking about CEOs or customers; start by naming the document each person
expects; choose what the sponsor likes
Make sure it is achievable
gut-check with someone who has done it; five options if not solvable (do it anyway,
recruit skills, reduce scope, move on, leave); checklist: we need this, boring and
obvious, no existing effort, support, agreed document, solvable by me, not lying to
myself
